articles.headline: Week 2 winners and losers: Tyler Shough, DeVonta Smith shine; Bijan Robinson struggles
articles.description: Tyler Shough and DeVonta Smith came up big in Week 2, while Bijan Robinson and Justin Jefferson had very quiet days.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 fantasy football season wasn't the high-scoring bonanza of last week, but DeVonta Smith, Ja'Marr Chase and Tyler Shough all came up big. On the flip side, fantasy stars Bijan Robinson, Justin Jefferson and Drake London all had disappointing games.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the opening week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 2

1. DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

If he's destined for a breakout, fantasy WR1-caliber year, this might well be the starting-point game his managers refer to. Smith scored 27.7 fantasy points, his sixth most in 82 career games, and he had a 38% target share. He's in prime position to shine, with A.J. Brown now in New England, and he'll get a fantastic Week 3 matchup in which to potentially repeat the effort versus the Chicago Bears. -- Cockcroft

2. Tyler Shough, QB, and Chris Olave, WR, New Orleans Saints

The Shough-Olave combination produced high-end numbers again in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. Shough (22.38 points) threw for 252 yards and a touchdown, while he rushed for 23 yards and another score on nine carries. That's two straight games for Shough with at least 22 points. Olave caught 8 of a team-high 10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, which was good for 22.6 points -- after dropping 28.2 points on the Lions in Week 1. Olave will remain a midtier WR1 for me in the ranks for the Week 3 matchup versus the Raiders, while Shough should be viewed as a fringe QB1. -- Bowen

3. Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Chase, who had a slow Week 1 start (3.2 points), bounced back in Sunday's win over the Texans, dropping 26.5 points on one of the league's best defenses. Chase caught 7 of 9 targets for 75 yards and added two touchdowns, one on a ridiculous snag that highlighted his hands, body control and focus. This is another reminder to trust your top picks after a tough ballgame. Talent wins. -- Bowen

4. Dalton Schultz, TE, Houston Texans

With Texans No. 1 wide receiver Nico Collins out with a hamstring injury, Schultz was the priority target for quarterback C.J. Stroud in Sunday's loss to the Bengals. Schultz totaled career highs in receptions (12), targets (14) and receiving yards (140). Schultz, who finished with 26.0 points (second most in his career), will be in the TE1 mix for the Week 3 game at Indianapolis if Collins is down again. Can't ignore that receiving usage. -- Bowen

5. Bryce Young, QB, and Darren Waller, TE, Carolina Panthers

This is the first time in Young's four-year NFL career that he has scored at least 20 fantasy points in back-to-back games, and his 31.44 points in Week 1 and 24.08 on Sunday are his third- and fifth-best outputs. articles.headline: Hurts taunts Titans after Eagles win: Finished what you started
articles.description: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons approached Jalen Hurts for a post-game dap-up following Philadelphia's 24-20 come-from-behind win Sunday and the Eagles quarterback was ready for him.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE - Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons approached Jalen Hurts for a post-game dap-up following Philadelphia's 24-20 come-from-behind win Sunday and the Eagles quarterback was ready for him.

"You started that s---," Hurts said with a smile, taking a break from his postgame interview to address Simmons. "I had to finish it."

The two exchanged words after that but Hurts made it clear that he had heard Simmons' comments to reporters earlier in the week, when Simmons told reporters: "We just need to make Jalen Hurts be a QB. Stop his runs, make sure Hurts doesn't get out of the pocket and make plays."

Hurts got the last word, engineering a nine-play, 65-yard drive in the closing minutes and hitting receiver Darius Cooper for a three-yard touchdown pass with nine seconds remaining to lift the Eagles to a 2-0 record.

"I love our guys so of course my natural instinct is, 'Oh, I want to fight,'" said coach Nick Sirianni after the game. "But when you get wrapped into the battle of words or revenge or whatever it is, anger, that s--- lasts about two minutes in a game. It does. At the end of the day, the fundamentals take over, the situational awareness takes over, you playing together as a team, your toughness takes over, because that all fades."

Simmons added further context to his original comments postgame.

"He's a Super Bowl MVP," Simmons said. "That wasn't no shot at Jalen. The thing was if we could keep him in the pocket and eliminate him from scrambling and running, making him go sideways, we could be successful especially getting them to third down.

"We saw Jalen would try to make something happen downfield and take off running. You see it all over his tape. That was my point of making Jalen Hurts stay in the pocket and just be a quarterback. It wasn't, 'Oh he can't be a quarterback in the pocket.'"

Hurts and the offense were not having the best day at the office. The Eagles QB had thrown two interceptions, the operation looked sluggish at times minus running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and behind a reconfigured offensive line working without left guard Landon Dickerson (knee). Tennessee went ahead by three on a field goal with six minutes remaining.

"Hey, let's finish. We've got them right where we want them," Hurts said before taking the field, according to Cooper.

Hurts went 5-of-7 on the final drive, including a 19-yarder to DeVonta Smith down the left sideline on 3rd-and-6 with 20 seconds remaining that put Philadelphia on the doorstep.

"He didn't flinch," Smith said of Hurts.

The next play was supposed to go to Smith as well, but the receiver lost his footing. Hurts' attention turned to Cooper, whose job was to run a pick for Smith on the play. He instead turned into the target and was able to haul in a high pass from Hurts in the back of the end zone. It was Cooper's first NFL touchdown and Hurts' first career go-ahead passing TD in the final minute of regulation or over

articles.headline: Alan Roden's 3-run homer, Dean Kremer's stellar start send Twins past Angels 8-0
articles.description: — Alan Roden hit a three-run homer and drove in a career-high four runs, and Dean Kremer yielded one hit over six stellar innings in the Minnesota Twins ' 8-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on...
articles.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. -- — Alan Roden hit a three-run homer and drove in a career-high four runs, and Dean Kremer yielded one hit over six stellar innings in the Minnesota Twins ' 8-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday.


              Josh Bell had three hits and two RBI for the Twins, who have won three of five overall after splitting four games at Angel Stadium with two shutout victories. Brooks Lee added three hits and scored three runs.


              Roden had three hits in his first major league game this month, punctuated by a shot to right in the seventh for his third career homer, his first since Aug. 6, 2025.


              Kremer (3-1) shut down the Angels in the third consecutive strong start by Minnesota's deadline acquisition. He walked three, but struck out eight for his most in a start since April.


              Minnesota allowed just two singles by the Angels, with Bailey Ober pitching the final three innings to earn his first career save.


              Ryan Johnson (5-9) yielded three runs on seven hits and couldn't get out of the fifth inning despite striking out six for the AL-worst Angels in the home finale of their 11th consecutive losing season and their 12th straight non-playoff campaign, both the longest active streaks in the majors.


              The game also was likely their last at Angel Stadium during the 24-year tenure of owner Arte Moreno, who intends to sell the team to Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke before next season begins.


              Bell and Roden singled in runs with two outs in the third, and Bell added another two-out RBI single in the fifth to chase Johnson.


              Emmanuel Rodriguez got credit for a double in the sixth even though Jose Siri dropped his catchable fly ball to the warning track in center. Rodriguez beat Siri's throw to score on a single by Ben Ross, who then stole second and scored when Zach Neto let the throw trickle into center.


              Up next
              Twins: Their final road series begins Monday night in San Francisco. Ober (7-6, 4.32 ERA) was slated to start before he took the mound in relief.


              Angels: Yusei Kikuchi (1-6, 5.02 ERA) makes the 13th start of his injury-plagued season in West Sacramento against the Athletics on Tuesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 2 games
articles.description: Will Aaron Rodgers stay QB1 all season? Is anything different for the Eagles' offense? And could the Lions miss the postseason again? We're judging Week 2 overreactions.
articles.body:
OK, so we all know we aren't supposed to overreact to Week 1 of the NFL season. But what about Week 2???

Is this enough data yet? Are we ready to crown the Bills as the team to beat? Are the Panthers truly an offensive juggernaut? Are teams out of their minds to not be hiring Brian Flores as a head coach? Is the Bengals' defense suddenly really good?

Yes, of course it's still too soon. And of course we still don't know anything. But we have twice as much information as we had a week ago, so why not dive in? It's our Week 2 overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational overreactions. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

Jump to:

Rodgers on thin ice?

Same Eagles offense?

Huge QB problems for Atlanta?

Flores should be a head coach?

Lions missing the playoffs?

Fantasy overreactions

Aaron Rodgers will get benched at some point this season

Rodgers came back for one more season with the Steelers, reunited with his old Packers coach Mike McCarthy. Neat story ... not such a neat offense so far.

The Steelers were sluggish in their Week 1 victory over the Falcons, and they were putrid Sunday in a 20-3 loss to the Patriots in Foxborough. The Patriots sacked Rodgers four times. One of those resulted in a fumble that New England ran back for a touchdown to effectively ice the game early in the fourth quarter.

Rodgers had no answer for New England's pressure, whether the Patriots were blitzing or not. He was 5-of-12 for 34 yards and four sacks when pressured Sunday. The Patriots blitzed him on 19 of 44 dropbacks, and Rodgers was 8-for-17 for 42 yards, two sacks and an interception on those. Through two games this season, Rodgers is completing 33% of his passes for an average of 3.5 yards per attempt when pressured. This is not sustainable, and the fact that Rodgers is 42 years old makes the extent to which he's getting pressured and hit all the more worrisome.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

I simply do not believe that McCarthy would bench Rodgers in his final season for Mason Rudolph, Will Howard or Drew Allar -- at least not until the Steelers are eliminated from postseason contention. These two guys reunited in Pittsburgh this year to pursue a championship together, and no matter what the rest of us think, they believe it's possible and won't give up the ghost until they have to.

Plus, you really can't lay Sunday's performance entirely at Rodgers' feet. The Steelers need to figure out a run game and some better protection schemes if they're going to keep Rodgers upright and have a chance this season. It's just too early to sit here and predict that they won't.

The Eagles' offense isn't any better than it was last season

articles.headline: 'Stayin Alive' Red Sox cap turnaround, clinch playoff spot
articles.description: The Red Sox are the fourth team to make the playoffs after being 14-or-more games under .500 in a season in the World Series era (since 1903).
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- As the Boston Red Sox celebrated an improbable postseason berth at Tropicana Field, with champagne and beer flowing all around, the clubhouse soundtrack seemed appropriate.

"Stayin' Alive.''

"I think that pretty much says it all,'' left fielder Roman Anthony said Sunday. "We pretty much stayed alive when nobody else thought we could. Now here we are.''

The Red Sox were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East race on June 24. They have since gone 52-25 and will be in the playoffs.

The Red Sox lost 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays in their series finale, so couldn't take care of things themselves. But about an hour after the game finished, the Houston Astros lost 4-2 to the Atlanta Braves, allowing the Red Sox to secure a wild-card spot.

Shortly after the Astros-Braves result went final, Red Sox players, coaches and staff members gathered near the Tropicana Field mound for a team photograph.

"I really don't care how we got in, as long as we got in,'' shortstop Trevor Story said.

The Red Sox are the fourth  team to make the playoffs after being 14-or-more games under .500 in a season in the World Series era (since 1903). Two of the three previous instances made the World Series, with the Boston Braves winning it in 1914. 

Interim manager Chad Tracy was in place for much of this year's turnaround. Since being appointed on April 26 following the dismissal of Alex Cora, the Red Sox have gone 74-55.

"Look, we were not in a good spot,'' Tracy said. "We were not playing good ball. But it shows you that if you stick to it, good things can happen. I couldn't be more proud of this group.''

First baseman Willson Contreras said he kept the faith, even when things trended downward, and the reward was sweet.

"It's hard not to have some tears over this,'' Contreras said. "It's a great accomplishment, but I don't want this team to stop here. I want to keep going. We have proven that you can get hot and overcome a lot of big odds.''

Information from ESPN Research and The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Tyler Shough, dubbed 'Poor man' by Saints, leads win vs. Ravens
articles.description: After Ravens DC Anthony Weaver attempted to pay Saints QB Tyler Shough a compliment by referring to him as a "poor man's Josh Allen," the New Orleans coaches turned it into a joke, dubbing Shough "Poor man" for the rest of the week.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver tried to pay New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough a compliment last week by referring to him as a "poor man's Josh Allen."

The Saints coaches turned it into a joke, dubbing Shough "Poor man" for the rest of the week.

"I loved it. I knew what he meant by it, but yeah, obviously he's an elite player, but it fires me up," Shough said after the Saints' 24-17 win over the Ravens. 

While the "poor man" portion of Weaver's comments went viral, he was trying to make a point that Shough impressed him last year when New Orleans played Miami, where Weaver was the defensive coordinator. Shough threw for two touchdowns in that game. 

"Has all the arm talent in the world [and] can run. I don't think he gets enough credit for how good [of] an athlete he is," Weaver said. " ... I just think the more reps he gets, the more confident he's going to get in that scheme and with the talent around him. I think they have done a good job of trying to build the talent around him. They have tremendous skill players. I think they have upgraded their offensive line from when I saw [them] a year ago. So, sky's the limit for the kid."

Shough turned the tables on the Ravens late in the fourth quarter Sunday, scoring a go-ahead touchdown on a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-goal with 1:32 remaining. The touchdown, which put the Saints up 24-17, was confirmed after officials said they could not find clear evidence on replay that he had not broken the plane of the goal line.

Allen's 11 fourth-quarter passing and rushing touchdowns are the most since Week 10 of last season. But Shough is not far behind, with his 10 such touchdowns trailing only Allen in that timespan. 

As of the end of Sunday's early games, Shough led the league with 662 passing yards, was tied for fifth with three passing touchdowns and was tied for fourth with one rushing touchdown.

"You know how social media be, but it's not really motivation, man. People try to compare people all the time, but I feel like Tyler's one of one," Saints wide receiver Chris Olave said. "He's making a name for himself in his league and by the end of the year, I feel like he's going to be one of the top quarterbacks."

articles.headline: Cronenworth homers twice, Padres beat Marlins 7-3 to lower wild-card magic number to 2
articles.description: Jake Cronenworth hit a pair of two-run homers and drove in five runs for the San Diego Padres, who beat the Miami Marlins 7-3 on Sunday to move closer to clinching their third straight postseason berth.
articles.body:
Jake Cronenworth hit a pair of two-run homers and drove in five runs for the San Diego Padres, who beat the Miami Marlins 7-3 on Sunday to move closer to clinching their third straight postseason berth. 


              Fernando Tatis Jr. hit his 25th homer for the Padres, who won for the 13th time in 14 games and swept the Marlins for the second time this season.


              San Diego reduced its magic number to two for earning a wild-card spot.


              The Padres and Cubs remain tied at 87-69 for the top wild-card spot with six games to go, although Chicago holds the tiebreaker. Philadelphia stayed one game back. 


              The top wild-card team will host a best-of-three opening series. The Cubs beat the Padres 2-1 in the wild-card round last year in Chicago.


              Cronenworth lofted a two-run shot into the home run porch in the right-field corner off Sandy Alcantara (13-11) with two outs in the second. 


              He connected again to right off Bradley Blalock with two outs in the eighth, his seventh. It was his second career multihomer game.


              Walker Buehler took a one-hitter and a 4-0 lead into the seventh before allowing Javier Sanoja's three-run homer to left with two outs, his 10th.


              That was it for Buehler (9-6), who allowed three runs and three hits while striking out six and walking two in a season-high 6 2/3 innings. He retired 11 straight at one point.


              Tatis homered into the Padres bullpen in left-center off Blalock leading off the seventh. It's his fourth career 25-homer season. 


              Cronenworth and Samad Taylor hit consecutive RBI singles in the fourth.


              Alcantara allowed four runs and eight hits in six innings, struck out three and walked one.


              Up next
              Marlins RHP Janson Junk (6-9, 4.50 ERA) is scheduled to start Tuesday night in the opener of a three-game series at the Chicago Cubs.


              The Padres haven't named a starter for Tuesday night's series opener at the Los Angeles Dodgers.


              ------

articles.headline: Cowboys' TD record: I caught a TD pass from Dak Prescott
articles.description: Prescott matched Tony Romo in the record book, so we sought the best moments from those who are helping him make history.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This story was originally published on Sept. 16. On Sunday, Dak Prescott tied Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in Dallas Cowboys history by throwing three against the Washington Commanders.

FRISCO, Texas -- Sometime soon, perhaps as soon as Sunday against the Washington Commanders, Dak Prescott will set another Dallas Cowboys record: most touchdown passes in team history.

He has 245, leaving him three shy of the 248 Tony Romo threw from 2006 to 2016.

"I might remember every single one of them," Prescott said.

His first?

"Slant to Dez in the fourth quarter against Chicago," Prescott said.

True. Prescott's first touchdown pass was a 17-yarder to receiver Dez Bryant in the third game of his rookie season after being selected in Round 4 of the 2016 draft. The Cowboys beat the Chicago Bears, giving Prescott his first career victory at AT&T Stadium.

His favorite?

"I don't think I have a true favorite, one that stands out," Prescott said. "Any of them that have been a game winner or some big-time, fourth-quarter touchdowns, those are the ones that stick out in my mind."

Needing four touchdown passes against the Commanders in the Cowboys' home opener at AT&T Stadium on Sunday (4:25 p.m. ET, Fox) might seem daunting, but Prescott has already reached that mark four times against Washington, the last coming in a 38-10 win in Week 18 of the 2023 season.

Prescott has thrown touchdowns to 39 different players, including 10 current teammates. CeeDee Lamb has the most with 35. Eleven have caught one.

Instead of Prescott's favorite touchdown passes, ESPN asked nine current and former teammates to describe their favorite scoring receptions from the quarterback, including Lamb and right tackle Terence Steele, whose only career catch is a TD from Prescott.

CeeDee Lamb, WR

Situation: Week 17, 2023, vs. Detroit Lions, first quarter, third-and-13 from Cowboys' 8

Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes should have sacked Prescott, but somehow he escaped at the goal line, drifted to his right and let go of a deep ball toward Lamb. Before he caught the pass, cornerback Kindle Vildor fell. Lamb caught the ball at midfield and was able to jog into the end zone for a 92-yard score.

"Dak did a great job of beating the blitz. I did a good job of expanding on the scramble drill," Lamb said. "We preach extending drives and extending plays and that was a big part of that. That was one of the longest plays of my career. For sure, my most favorite."

It was the longest completion of Prescott's career, the longest catch of Lamb's and the second-longest completion in team history. It was also Lamb's 111th catch of the season, which tied him for Michael Irvin's team record for most in a season, which he later broke.

Has he ever run that far without being chased?

"Nah, I don't think I'll ever get that close to it again. Great time," Lamb said. "I enjoyed it. As you could tell, I trotted in the end zone. It was fire."
